notes:
POC focused on Dedicated reserved capacity for contract search and high-throughput document ingestion.
- Primary ask: throughput guarantee for peak hours (target sustained 1.2M tokens/hour, bursts to 3M tokens/hour).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for 512-token generation; p99 < 600ms for heavy reranking workloads.
- QoS: strict tail-latency budget—app will degrade gracefully to a lighter quantized model when p99 exceeds threshold.
- Hardware preference: H100-backed pools for encoding/long-context tasks; exploring mixed pool (A100 + H100) for cost tradeoffs.
- Cache strategy: prefix KV cache required (repetitive contract sections); want baseline hit-rate > 30% during soak.
- Batching: need recommendations for batching windows to hit throughput without violating latency SLOs.
- Soak test plan: 72-hour continuous ingest at 80% expected traffic, with hourly spikes to 120% for 10 minutes.
- Load test plan: synthetic workload using 4 representative prompt families (contract search, clause extraction, Q&A, summarization) with token length distributions matching production.
- Metrics tracked: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, requests/sec, GPU % utilization, queue depth, batch sizes, KV cache hits, memory pressure, error rates.
- SLA negotiation notes: they want 99.95% availability, credits for missed SLOs, clear definitions for 'service downtime' vs 'degraded performance'.
- Interested in reserved GPU planning: target pool of 12 H100 GPUs initially, with autoscaling headroom for 25% burst.
- Security: require SAML SSO, syslogs to customer SIEM, audit logs retention 12 months, optional on-prem control plane.
- Data residency: EU contract subset to remain on EU-only pool; legal to produce addendum.
- Questions from security call: encryption keys lifecycle, backup retention, on-prem installer checklist.
- Quote from CTO: "We need predictable latency under heavy ingestion—can't have tail spikes during contract review windows."
- Commercial: procurement needs an outline of reserved commit tiers, cancellation terms, and demo of cost modeling (Optimize recommendations).
- Internal risk: existing infra team prefers self-host but lacks ops to guarantee p99; Redwood Dedicated is the leading option if SLA and KMS integrate.
- POC acceptance criteria draft: sustained throughput goal hit for 72h soak, latency SLOs met at p95/p99 during 95% of windows, KMS integration validated, EU residency proof-of-isolation.
- Next follow-ups: schedule SLA workshop, get security team the on-prem checklist, agreed load test script repo (drive link).
